extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of aesthetics, artists, critics, and philosophers interested in Kantian theories of art
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for producing and judging 'beautiful art' as laid out in Kant's Critique of the Power of Judgement: what counts as genius, taste, spirit, and the distinguishing features of different arts (poetry, rhetoric, painting, sculpture, music, architecture, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirit (animating principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spirit, in an aesthetical sense, is the name given to the animating principle of the mind; that whereby this principle animates the soul is the material which it applies so as to put the mental powers purposively into swing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works may be neat and elegant yet 'without spirit' (e.g., a history exact and well arranged but lacking vivacity). Spirit is what quickens the mind and sustains the play of cognitive powers; it is cultivated by the presentation of aesthetical Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetical Idea is a representation of the Imagination which occasions much thought, without any definite thought (i.e., any concept) being capable of being adequate to it; it cannot be completely compassed and made intelligible by language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetical Ideas are the source of 'spirit' in art: they give a multiplicity of kindred representations that arouse more thought than can be expressed by a determinate concept (examples: poetic presentations of eternity, death, the kingdom of the blessed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of Imagination and Understanding (genius)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius consists in the happy relation between the Imagination and the Understanding: Imagination furnishes undeveloped material and Understanding supplies the concept/purpose; genius finds Ideas for a given concept and expresses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius is a natural talent that cannot be taught by science or industry; it supplies original Ideas and their expression (the latter often called 'spirit').

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression (making the ineffable communicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The talent to express the ineffable element of a subjective state of mind and to make it universally communicable—seizing the play of Imagination and unifying it in a concept which discloses a new rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expression is distinct from the mere presence of Ideas; a work must not only contain aesthetical Ideas but also express them so others can share the feeling. This expressive talent is often what people call 'spirit'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free purposiveness (unsought subjective purposiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unsought undesigned subjective purposiveness in the free accordance of the Imagination with the legality of the Understanding: art should appear free from rule-following yet purposive relative to the concept of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beautiful art must seem undesigned and not the product of mechanical imitation or pre-given rules; rule-following that dominates destroys the aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste (judgement) as discipline of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste, like Judgement in general, is the discipline (or training) of Genius; it clips its wings, makes it cultured and polished, brings clearness and order into many thoughts, and makes Ideas susceptible of universal assent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste adjusts the freedom and wealth of the Imagination to the Understanding; for beautiful art both Imagination and Judgement are requisite, and Taste is the indispensable condition (conditio sine qua non).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of Taste over Genius for beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Though abundance and originality of Ideas (genius) enrich art, accordance of the Imagination in its freedom with the conformity to law of the Understanding (Taste/Judgement) is more important for being beautiful art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict must arise, the Judgement will rather sacrifice freedom and wealth of Imagination than permit anything prejudicial to the Understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality as exemplary, not imitable
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of a genius is an example to be followed by another genius but not imitated; imitation that copies a genius's peculiarities down to deformities is mere aping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius is exemplary because it awakens originality in others; slavish copying destroys the spirit and becomes a fault rather than an honourable method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mannerism vs Method
rubrics_metrics.description: Manner (modus aestheticus) has no other standard than the feeling of unity in presentation and differs from method (modus logicus) which follows definite principles; mannerism is exposition founded on singularity rather than on adequacy to the Idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mannerism (ostentatious, contorted, affected style adopted to differentiate oneself) betrays a bungler; true aesthetic manner should be appropriate to the Idea, not mere peculiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being 'studied and anxious'—freedom in art
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art must be free art in a double sense: it is not tradesman-like (quantifiable by standards) and the mind feels content without ulterior purpose; all that is studied and anxious must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The art must appear spontaneous and not contrived for reward or external ends; contrivance undermines the aesthetic free play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical attributes (symbols that quicken imagination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetical attributes are representations that do not constitute the concept but express consequences and relations that open the Imagination onto many kindred representations (e.g., Jupiter's eagle as attribute of the king of heaven).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such attributes enliven the mind by suggesting an illimitable field of associations and serve as substitutes for logical presentation when the rational Idea cannot be adequately presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form must be purposive for judgement (form over mere sensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential element in beautiful art is the form which is purposive as regards our observation and judgement; matter that is mere sensation (charm or emotion) leaves nothing in the Idea and leads to mere enjoyment rather than cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art that only gratifies sensations makes the spirit dull; beautiful art should cultivate the mind by linking pleasure with Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of arts by mode of expression: speech, deportment, tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful arts divide according to the analogy with speech's modes of expression: word (speech), deportment (formative arts), and tone (play of sensations). The arts of SPEECH are rhetoric and poetry; FORMATIVE arts include plastic (sculpture, architecture) and painting; PLAY OF SENSATIONS includes music and art of colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each class has its own standards: rhetoric/poetry must balance play and business of Understanding; formative arts must consider sensible truth vs illusion; play of sensations requires proportion and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric vs Poetry: honesty and function
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the art of carrying on a serious business of the Understanding as if it were a free play of Imagination; poetry conducts a free play of Imagination as if it were serious business of the Understanding. Poetry declares itself as play and thus 'proceeds with honesty and candour'; rhetoric as persuasion may deceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhetoric (ars oratoria) used to captivate be judged dialectic/potentially objectionable in contexts requiring truthfulness (law, pulpit); poetry's honesty makes it higher in aesthetic rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plastic art (sculpture) vs Architecture: sensible truth vs use
rubrics_metrics.description: Plastic arts (sculpture) present corporeal concepts as they might have existed in nature (sensible truth); Architecture presents concepts possible only through art with an essential point being a certain use of the artistic object (utility determines architectural form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In sculpture the main design is expression of aesthetical Ideas; in architecture suitability for use is essential; house furniture and useful objects fall under architecture because of their use-determined form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting vs landscape gardening: sensible illusion vs beautiful arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting provides the illusory appearance of corporeal extension (depicting nature); the beautiful arrangement of nature's products (landscape gardening) gives an appearance of utility and availableness for other purposes than mere play of the Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decorative combinations (rooms, finery) are judged by forms as they present themselves to the eye, aimed at entertainment of the Imagination without definite purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and art of colour: play of sensations and proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of the beautiful play of sensations concerns proportions (tone) in hearing and sight; music may be the beautiful play of sensations (or merely pleasant) but involves a mathematical element enabling judgement about proportions of vibrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion/harmony and alternation prevent impressions from destroying one another and produce sustained animation of the mind; however, music often produces transitory enjoyment rather than permanent cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence vs transitoriness of impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative arts (painting, sculpture, architecture) produce permanent impressions that serve as vehicles for concepts; music and pure play of sensations produce transitory impressions which more readily lead to weariness on repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cultivation of mind, permanence that allows recall and further reflection is of higher worth than fleeting sensory charm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical condition in music as necessary but not sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematical element (relation between vibrations) is the indispensible condition (conditio sine qua non) enabling judgement of proportion in music, but mathematics alone does not account for music's charm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion allows Taste to claim authority over judgement, yet the affective power of music goes beyond mere mathematical relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of arts: artistic enhancement vs possible loss of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful arts can be combined (e.g., rhetoric with theatrical presentation, poetry with music to make an opera), often making art more artistic, but not necessarily more beautiful because multiple satisfactions may cross one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In combinations the essential element remains form purposive for judgement and cultivation; mere aggregation of pleasures may diminish the aesthetic value if form/purpose is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against art as distraction from moral/cultural ends
rubrics_metrics.description: If beautiful arts are not brought into close combination with moral Ideas (which alone bring self-sufficing satisfaction) they risk becoming mere distraction that ultimately renders the mind more discontented and useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beauties of nature and morally oriented art are of most benefit when they accustom one to observation, appreciation, and admiration leading to inner cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking arts by capacity to cultivate the mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry ranks first (expands Imagination and cultivates faculties), tone/music is powerful for charm and movement but lowest for cultivation, formative arts rank higher than music for promoting permanent concepts and urbanity of higher cognitive powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an art's aesthetic worth consider its contribution to the enlargement and culture of cognitive faculties, not merely its immediate pleasurable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid aping and slavish imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation becomes mere aping when the scholar copies everything including deformities that a genius let pass; mannerism also is a species of aping—mere peculiarity lacking exemplary talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should follow the spirit or example (awaken originality) rather than copy surface singularities; contrived peculiarity signals lack of genuine talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as communicative play vs tradesman product
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art should be a free play that entertains the Imagination while also providing food for the Understanding; it is not a tradesman's work, whose magnitude can be judged, exacted, or paid for according to a definite standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art must provide purposive occupation of faculties without being accountable to market-like measures of production and should avoid promising what it does not deliver.
